title: SAML IdP-Initiated Single Logout
subtitle: The user signs out at the IdP portal; the IdP kills its own session first, then fans a signed LogoutRequest out to every participant SP and reports the aggregate result.

steps.label: Click Sign out on the IdP portal
steps.lede: The user ends their session from the IdP itself. There is no initiating SP LogoutRequest here — the IdP is the origin of the logout.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log and Disable cache. Hidden-iframe fan-out is easy to miss — Preserve log is what keeps those iframe requests visible.

steps.label: IdP ends its session and fans out
steps.lede: The IdP terminates its own session first, identifies the participants (here SP and SP2) with their per-SP NameID + SessionIndex, and returns a page embedding one hidden iframe per SP SLO endpoint.

resp.json: <html><body>IdP session ended; fanning out LogoutRequests via hidden iframes</body></html>

steps.devtools: The IdP kills its session before propagation so a broken chain can never leave the IdP session alive. The response embeds one hidden iframe per participant SP — each will issue its own SAMLRequest.

steps.label: LogoutRequest to SP (hidden iframe)
steps.lede: One iframe loads the SP's SLO endpoint with a signed LogoutRequest. The SP verifies it, destroys the session, and expires its cookie, then redirects the iframe back to the IdP with a LogoutResponse.
steps.codeTitle: Redirect binding — decode the SAMLRequest (a LogoutRequest)
steps.code:
URL-decode → base64-decode → INFLATE (raw DEFLATE)

<samlp:LogoutRequest
    ID="_synthetic-lor-00000000000000000000000001"
    Version="2.0"
    IssueInstant="2026-07-25T16:00:00Z"
    Destination="https://idp.example.net/slo/redirect">
  <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.net/saml/metadata</saml:Issuer>
  <saml:NameID Format="…:persistent">S-1-5-21-SYNTHETIC-USER-abc123</saml:NameID>
  <samlp:SessionIndex>_synthetic-session-0000000000001</samlp:SessionIndex>
</samlp:LogoutRequest>
steps.devtools: The iframe request shows Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe. URL-decode → base64-decode → INFLATE the SAMLRequest to read the LogoutRequest; note the SP clears its cookie with Max-Age=0. Use SAML Tracer / Auth Inspector to auto-decode.

steps.label: LogoutRequest to SP2 (parallel iframe)
steps.lede: A second hidden iframe hits SP2's SLO endpoint at the same time. Parallel iframes are faster than a redirect chain but lose confirmations whenever browsers block third-party frames or cookies.
steps.devtools: Treat a missing LogoutResponse as a failure: a blocked third-party frame or cookie means the request may start but the session is never cleared — a silent partial logout. Back-channel SOAP fan-out, when used instead, is server-to-server and invisible here.

steps.label: LogoutResponses return to the IdP
steps.lede: Each iframe redirects back to the IdP carrying that SP's LogoutResponse. The IdP correlates them by InResponseTo and aggregates the Status values.
steps.devtools: Base64-decode (or inflate, for the Redirect binding) each SAMLResponse and read Status. The Issuer is now the responding SP, and InResponseTo echoes the IdP's per-SP LogoutRequest ID.

steps.label: Aggregate result page
steps.lede: The IdP renders its own result — unlike SP-initiated SLO there is no final LogoutResponse to an SP. If every participant confirmed, the user is signed out of all applications.
steps.devtools: Nothing further on the wire. If any SP timed out or its LogoutResponse was lost, the IdP reports PartialLogout and advises closing the browser to be safe.
